question: If the median of a data is 46.36 less than its mode, then the median of the data exceeds its mean by______. (Use the empirical formula)
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Use the direct **Empirical Formula** relation: **Mode − Median = 2 × (Median − Mean)**.

Given: **Mode − Median = 46.36**.

Substitute the value: 46.36 = 2 × (Median − Mean).

Median − Mean = 46.36 ÷ 2 = 23.18.

**∴ The correct answer is 23.18.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Median = Mode − 46.36 ⇒ **Mode − Median = 46.36**.

**Formula:** The empirical relationship between **Mean**, **Median**, and **Mode** is **Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d8e18f6c9d7d18f5dd7cfbf30c3c175d92c69bf785f31d9bc475af1eacb44600.png] 

⇒ Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean

⇒ Mode − Median = (3 × Median − 2 × Mean) − Median

⇒ Mode − Median = 2 × Median − 2 × Mean

⇒ 46.36 = 2 × (Median − Mean)

⇒ Median − Mean = 46.36 ÷ 2

⇒ Median − Mean = 23.18

**∴ The correct answer is 23.18.**

**__Additional Information__**

Empirical Formula

For a **moderately skewed distribution**, the relationship is **Mode = 3 Median − 2 Mean**.

Symmetric Distribution

In a perfectly **symmetrical distribution**, the Mean, Median, and Mode are all equal (**Mean = Median = Mode**).

Mean-Mode Relation

The difference **Mean − Mode = 3 × (Mean − Median)** is another common form of this empirical rule.</p
